turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: I warn you, Sandip, that I will not hesitate to take action against any further oppression of my tenantry. You would do well to heed my words, lest you suffer the consequences.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: You, too, should not forget your own role in all this, Nikhil. The oppressed tenantry are merely pawns in your game of power, aren't they?

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: I am not playing with pawns, Sandip. I am a zamindar, and I will not have my people mistreated.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: You'd do better to worry about your own crumbling estate, Nikhil, rather than lecturing me on how to run mine.

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: Your estate may be crumbling, Sandip, but at least it is not built on the suffering of my tenantry, who have been loyal to me and my family for generations.

turns.speaker: Bimala
turns.text: Sandip, perhaps we could discuss this further, away from Nikhil's presence?

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Oh, Nikhil, always so full of passion for the welfare of your tenantry, but I see no tears for the state of your own crops, parched and withering like the soul of a zamindar who's lost his touch.

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: I will not be lectured by you on my duties as a zamindar, Sandip. My crops may be withering, but at least I have not sold my soul to the local Mussulmans, as I fear you have.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Well, Nikhil, it seems you're still peddling the same old tired tales of my supposed betrayal. If I've sold my soul, it's to the poetry of the Mughals, not to any Mussulman's purse.

turns.speaker: Bimala
turns.text: Sandip, perhaps it would be wise to listen to Nikhil, even if only to gauge the sincerity of his words.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Oh, Bimala, always the voice of reason, but I think I can handle Nikhil's dire warnings without your intervention. Or can I, my dear, you're starting to sound like my own conscience, and I'm not sure I like that.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Ah, Bimala, my dear, don't worry about me, I'll not be swayed by Nikhil's threats, I've got the loyalty of my own villagers, and a good dose of poetic license to keep me safe from any would-be attackers.

turns.speaker: Bimala
turns.text: Sandip, I think you're underestimating the gravity of Nikhil's words. His concerns may not be entirely unfounded.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Well, well, Nikhil, it seems your warnings have all the subtlety of a sledgehammer. Can't you see I'm in the midst of crafting a masterpiece, a poem that will outlast your petty threats and your flailing attempts at power?

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: I will not indulge in frivolous discussions about poetry or power, Sandip. The safety of our villagers is at stake, and I demand that you take my warnings seriously.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Oh, Nikhil, I'm shocked, simply shocked, that you'd stoop to using words like 'demand' in a conversation with a poet of my stature. I'll not be swayed by your threats, nor will I be intimidated by your pompous attitude.

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: I warn you, Sandip, not to trifle with the safety of our people. I will not be dismissed so easily, and I expect you to take concrete measures to address the concerns I have raised.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Ah, Nikhil, so you're still clinging to your delusions of grandeur, thinking you can dictate what I do with my own land and my own people? I think you'll find that I'm not quite the pushover you seem to think I am.

turns.speaker: Bimala
turns.text: I couldn't help but wonder, Nikhil, what specific measures you suggest we take to address the concerns you've raised?

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: I suggest we increase the number of guards in the village and establish a system of messengers to alert us in case of any potential threats. This is not a matter for poetic flourishes or personal pride, but a serious effort to protect the people who depend on us.

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: I say, Nikhil, don't you keep Browning among your books here? I was just telling Queen Bee of our college club. Do you remember that contest of ours over the translation of those lines from Browning? You don't?

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: I managed to get together the words to render it into Bengali, somehow, but the result was hardly likely to be a 'joy forever' to the people of Bengal. I really did think at one time that I was on the verge of becoming a poet, but Providence was kind enough to save me from that disaster. Do you remember old Dakshina? If he had not become a Salt Inspector, he would have been a poet. I remember his rendering to this day ...

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: No, Queen Bee, it is no use rummaging those bookshelves. Nikhil has ceased to read poetry since his marriage--perhaps he has no further need for it. But I suppose 'the fever fit of poesy', as the Sanskrit has it, is about to attack me again.

opening.speaker: Nikhil
opening.text: I have come to give you a warning, Sandip

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: About the fever fit of poesy?

opening.speaker: Nikhil
opening.text: For some time, Mahomedan preachers have been about stirring up the local Mussulmans. They are all wild with you, and may attack you any moment.

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: Are you come to advise flight?

opening.speaker: Nikhil
opening.text: I have come to give you information, not to offer advice.

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: Had these estates been mine, such a warning would have been necessary for the preachers, not for me. If, instead of trying to frighten me, you give them a taste of your intimidation, that would be worthier both of you and me. Do you know that your weakness is weakening your neighbouring zamindars also?

opening.speaker: Nikhil
opening.text: I did not offer you my advice, Sandip. I wish you, too, would refrain from giving me yours. Besides, it is useless. And there is another thing I want to tell you. You and your followers have been secretly worrying and oppressing my tenantry. I cannot allow that any longer. So I must ask you to leave my territory.

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: For fear of the Mussulmans, or is there any other fear you have to threaten me with?
